rows.en:
...The seventh one wasn't coming.
Waiting any longer would only be a waste of time.
The six who had come for me were fidgeting too, clearly wanting to go home.
...But I couldn't shake this uneasy feeling in my chest.
What was this foreboding?
I couldn't shake the sense that something was about to happen.
Would it be something good...
Or something bad...?
Everyone's eyes gathered on me.
All the stories were over.
Everyone was waiting for me to speak.{p}What should I do?
Suggest we all go home
Suggest we wait a little longer

"...Um.
Everyone, thank you so much for today.
It's a shame the seventh person didn't come, but I got to hear some really scary stories, so I think I can write a good article.
It's getting late, and I hate to ask, but...
Um, everyone, could you possibly spare me a little more of your time?"
I couldn't find the right words.
How could I explain this uneasy feeling?
Everyone listened to me, looking surprised.{p}

"...Why should we have to stay?
Do you have some lead on the seventh one, then?
If not, I'd rather you didn't tie me down.
I don't belong to you, after all."
It was Iwashita.
Keeping her head down, she glared up at me from under her brows.
Her eyes were so defiant that they overpowered me.{p}

...The mood had turned ugly.
Maybe I shouldn't have said that.
What should I do?{p}Should I take it back?
Let's go home after all
Sorry. Please stay a while longer

"I'm sorry.
Could you please stay here, even just a little longer?"{p}

"Why?"
It was Shindo.
"What's the reason?
The seventh one isn't coming. Our stories are done.
You shouldn't need us anymore.
So why the hell do we have to stick around?
Give me a reason."
Shindo seemed a little ticked off, too.
"...There's no reason.
I just have this strange, uneasy feeling.
Like, for some reason, we have to stay here..."{p}

"This is pointless, you know.
Unlike you, I happen to be a busy man.
I'll be taking my leave."
It was Kazama who cut in, instead of Shindo.{p}

Kazama was right.
I couldn't keep everyone here with no clear reason, just because of my own uneasy feeling.{p}

"See ya. So long."
Shindo got up from his seat.{p}

"...Sorry, {a}.
I'm going home too."
Then Fukuzawa, too.
After her, Kazama and Iwashita got up as well.{p}

Only Hosoda and Arai stayed in their seats, watching me.
Did these two feel the same unease I did?{p}
"See ya."
Shindo said it once more and opened the club room door.{p}

"Whoa!"
Shindo suddenly jumped.{p}

"Sanae!"
The moment Fukuzawa saw the girl standing there, blocking the doorway, she poked her head out from behind Shindo.{p}
...Sanae?{p}Sanae... Wasn't she...
I remember Sanae
Who's Sanae?

Sanae... Was she that strange girl Fukuzawa had told us about?
The strange girl who supposedly had old men and old women living inside her body, telling her about tests and things that were going to happen.
Why was she here...?
Don't tell me she was the seventh one?{p}

She didn't answer Fukuzawa. Instead, she looked around at each of us in turn, as if sizing us up.
And the moment her eyes met mine, she froze completely.
"...Are you {a}?"
She gave off a really strange impression.
Maybe Fukuzawa had been right about her.
...What should I do?{p}Should I just admit it?
Answer yes
Answer no

"...Uh, yes."
I hesitated a little, but decided to answer honestly.{p}

Then her eyes traveled over me, from the top of my head to the tips of my toes.
"Huh?"
For a moment, what she meant didn't sink in.
"Don't go home!"
Did she have eyes in the back of her head?
She suddenly spun around and sharply called out to Shindo, who was about to walk out the door.
Shindo turned around with a puzzled look, but grudgingly drew back the foot he had stepped out with.{p}

"Hey, look.
I'm going home now.
Unless you're the seventh one and you're gonna tell us the last story, that is."
He seemed pretty irritated at being sassed by a first-year like her.
"I'm not the seventh one."
"Then I'm leaving."
"If you leave now, you'll die."{p}

She said something that dangerous without batting an eye.
That was enough to stop Shindo in his tracks.
"I'm gonna die...?
Keep up the sick jokes and I'm gonna get mad for real."
No matter how Shindo tried to intimidate her, she kept talking back, perfectly calm.{p}

"Yes, they're coming.
To kill someone in this room."
Then she looked at me and smiled sweetly.
...Someone's going to be killed?
Hold on a minute.
Please don't say things like that with a smile.
"Oh, Reiko!"
When she spotted Fukuzawa, she went over to her, and they clasped hands.
Fukuzawa had called out to her, so had she really not noticed her until now?
"Wow, you're here too, Reiko.
Good for you, not getting killed."{p}

"Geez, Sanae, you're always like this.
Didn't you notice me waving at you?"
"I didn't notice.
Grandma didn't tell me about that."
...The two of them were having a conversation that made no sense to me.
I didn't think I could keep up with them.{p}

"...Would you two move?
Dying, being killed, none of it has anything to do with me.
I'll be going home now."
With that, Iwashita pushed her way between the two of them.{p}
"You're going to die, you know."{p}

"Me?
Heh heh... You're saying I'll be killed?
If anyone like that exists, I'll kill them first, before I ever die.
Instead of worrying about other people, you should worry about yourself."
Iwashita's face was smiling, but her eyes were terribly cold.{p}

Then she pushed Iwashita back as she tried to leave, and shut the club room door.
"Everyone, please go back to your seats."
There was a strange force about her.
Fukuzawa sat back down right away.
Kazama threw up his hands and tilted his head, as if to say "I can't believe this," then sighed and went back to the seat he'd been sitting in.
Shindo and Iwashita went back to their seats in sullen silence.
And once she had made sure everyone was seated, Sanae... I mean, Motoki sat down in the seat that had been set out for the seventh person.{p}

"I'll tell the last story.
{a}, is that okay?"
Motoki asked for my approval.{p}What should I do?
Please go ahead
No, if the seventh one is coming, let's wait
"Oh, please go ah..."{p}

"Wait a sec."
It was Fukuzawa who stopped me mid-sentence.
"Hey, Sanae.
There's something I want to ask you first.
Did I ever tell you about this meeting today?"{p}

Motoki quietly shook her head.
"Nuh-uh.
But Grandma told me.
She said if I didn't hurry over, something terrible would happen."
...Motoki really was unhinged.
Her eyes had a faraway, crazed look.
Should I really go on and listen to her story?{p}

...Could it be that the uneasy feeling I'd had was about Motoki?
Had she seen right through what I was thinking?{p}
Suddenly, she stared hard at my face.{p}

"Oh, that's right.
{a}, I forgot to tell you something important.
The reason I came here was to save you.
{a}, you and I are going to get married, apparently.
So Grandma told me to go save you.
If you die, I'll never be able to get married my whole life."
What?!★
Me, marry this girl?
Grandma said so?
...Maybe I should have gone home after all.{p}

...Oh no. Kazama and Shindo were both looking at me with big grins.
That was a far cry from the sulky faces they'd had a minute ago, but...{p}
What did telling the seventh story have to do with saving me?{p}What was I supposed to say to that?
Say "I'll marry you" from the bottom of my heart
Say "I'll marry you," even if it's a lie
Say I can't promise something like that

...I couldn't hurt Motoki's feelings in front of everyone.
Besides, if what she said was true, she had gone out of her way and taken a risk to come here for my sake.
She was a little unhinged, but wasn't that part of her charm, too?
...And it wasn't as if we were getting married right now.
If there really was a red thread of fate in this world, maybe a meeting like this wasn't so bad.
I made up my mind.{p}
When I said that, a cheer went up all around me.{p}

"Wow, way to go, {a}!
You're marrying Sanae!
You'd better invite me to the wedding!"
Fukuzawa was cackling.{p}

"Wow, I sure got to see something amazing.
I came here thinking I'd be telling scary stories, but somehow I got to see something really nice you hardly ever get to see.
Oh, jeez..."
Hosoda scratched his head, blushing.
It was as if he thought he was the one who'd gotten a love confession.{p}

"It's good to settle your life early.
For a commoner like you, planning your life out early is vital.
I'll be rooting for you, too.
You make a fine couple, ah ha ha ha ha..."
Kazama was saying whatever he pleased, since it was no concern of his.{p}

Shindo just kept smirking.
Iwashita and Arai kept their heads down, looking uninterested.{p}

...Nice to meet you, everyone.
You might already know about me from Reiko's story, but I'll introduce myself anyway.
My name is Sanae Motoki, and I'm a first-year.
I'll tell the last story before the seventh one comes.
This is a story I heard from my grandma.{p}

My grandma lives inside me, and she knows all kinds of things.
Sometimes she slips out of my body.
And then she goes and sees all sorts of stuff.
This is something that grandma saw.
It happened just recently.{p}

There was a student at this school named Takuro Kanda.
Kanda had a girlfriend.
She was super jealous.
So she kept Kanda on a tight leash.
She'd call him every night to check if he was home, and grill him about everything he'd done that day.
If a girl so much as came near him, she'd question him over and over, or throw a hysterical fit and get insanely angry.
Kanda got scared of her.
And he started wanting to break up with her.{p}

Right around then, a girl showed up who said she liked Kanda.
And that girl started getting close to Kanda.
Of course, when the jealous girlfriend found out, she got really, really angry.
But Kanda started going out with the girl behind her back anyway.{p}

But, see, there was someone who had a one-sided crush on that girl.
He hated Kanda's guts.
...A few days after that, Kanda died.
He died on the train tracks.
He used the rail as a pillow, took sleeping pills, and fell asleep right there.
Then a train came along, and its wheels ran over his head, and he died.
His head was crushed to a pulp, so badly they couldn't put it back together.
It was written off as suicide, but nobody knows if that's the truth.{p}

"That was booooring!"
The moment Motoki's story ended, Shindo was the one who yelled it.
Iwashita gave a snort of laughter.
...True, compared with the stories I'd heard so far, it didn't really have much of a point, and I couldn't call it interesting by any means.
...Then again, compared with Kazama's story, it was plenty scary.
But what did that story have to do with me being saved?
Maybe I'd been taken in by one of Motoki's jokes.{p}
